## How often: the seismic hazard curve

The seismic hazard curve $H(a)$ gives the mean number of times per year that the peak ground acceleration (PGA) at a site exceeds $a$. Its unit is per year. For example, $H(a) = 10^{-4}$ /yr means that shaking stronger than $a$ occurs on average once every 10,000 years.

::: {.callout-note title="Gal"}
A unit of acceleration: 1 Gal = 1 cm/s². Gravitational acceleration is about 980 Gal.
:::

## How fragile: the fragility curve

A fragility curve gives the conditional probability that a component fails when it experiences shaking of strength $a$. If the component capacity $R$ is lognormally distributed, the curve is [@kennedy1984]

$$
P_f(a) = \Pr[R \leq a] = \Phi\!\left(\frac{\ln(a/A_m)}{\beta}\right)
$$

where $A_m$ is the median capacity, $\beta$ is the logarithmic standard deviation, and $\Phi$ is the standard normal CDF. At $a = A_m$ the failure probability is exactly 0.5.

## Combining the two

Weighting the failure probability at each level of shaking by how often that shaking occurs, and summing, gives the annual failure frequency $\nu$.

$$
\nu = \int_0^{\infty} P_f(a)\,\left|\frac{\mathrm{d}H(a)}{\mathrm{d}a}\right|\,\mathrm{d}a
$$

A real assessment repeats this calculation for each accident sequence, which describes the combinations of failed components that lead to core damage.

## A measure of margin: HCLPF

The median alone does not show how much margin a component has, so the HCLPF (High Confidence of Low Probability of Failure) capacity is widely used. It is the acceleration at which there is 95% confidence that the failure probability is at most 5%, and it is approximated by the expression below. $\beta_R$ and $\beta_U$ are explained in the [next article](aleatory-epistemic.qmd).

$$
a_{\mathrm{HCLPF}} \approx A_m \exp\{-1.645\,(\beta_R + \beta_U)\}
$$

| Component        | $A_m$ [Gal] | $\beta_R$ | $\beta_U$ | $\beta_C$ | HCLPF [Gal] |
|:-----------------|-----------:|-----:|-----:|------:|------------:|
| Pump             |        980 | 0.30 | 0.35 | 0.461 |         336 |
| Electrical panel |      1,250 | 0.25 | 0.45 | 0.515 |         395 |
| Piping           |      1,600 | 0.28 | 0.32 | 0.425 |         596 |

: Example component parameters and HCLPF {#tbl-params}

The electrical panel's median is about 1.3 times the pump's, but its larger $\beta_R + \beta_U$ shrinks the HCLPF ratio to about 1.2.
